messages:
Maria: quick heads-up — flipped a 10% canary for the new dynamic token lasso (route-tier SLO governor) to staging at 11:03 PT, running soak + perf traces.
Ajay: any obvious regressions?
Maria: baseline p95 for /chat (prod-tier) was ~195ms. after enabling the token cap logic, p95 jumped to ~280-320ms on the affected hosts. median largely unchanged.
Taylor: did the kernel selector flip? the gating can cause fallback to the generic matmul path if sequence shapes change.
Maria: timeline shows kernel switch coincident with microbatch formation. sample trace: 
Maria: ```
[perf] batch_id=4821 host=i-0abc kernel=matmul_generic seq_len=256 kv_hit=0.12
latencies: per_token=6.3ms -> p95_step=300ms
```
Ajay: kv hit rate 12% is low. did the token budget change cause higher KV churn / cache evictions?
Maria: config diff: dynamic-token-bins reduced per-session token budget from 1024 -> 640 for prod-tier on the canary. That increases new-session admissions and reduces prefix reuse, so more new entries in KV.
Taylor: that would explain more cache misses -> longer runtime paths and larger effective sequences in formed batches -> kernel fallback and p95 spike. :thinking:
Ops-bot: deploybot posted: canary rolled at 7300000123 by maria
Lena: can we reproduce locally with the sim bench? try `./bench -route /chat -seq 256 -kv 0.1 -tokens 640` and capture the batcher logs.
Maria: ran the sim; it reproduces. condensed logs: 
Maria: ```
BATCHER: formed 8 microbatches (avg_seq=254) -> chosen_path=generic
RUNTIME: kv_miss_rate=0.88 prefetch_skipped=0.23
```
Ajay: options: a) revert the per-session budget and add a per-second admission cap to limit new-token churn, b) keep lower budget but tighten token-sculptor so it doesn't over-admit in short windows, or c) add queue-weight throttle for prod-tier to limit throughput while KV warms.
Taylor: also consider kernel-affinity hints: prefer the fp16-optimized kernel when seq<=128; for larger seqs, split microbatches or enforce max_microbatch_seq so we don't force the generic path.
Maria: quick mitigation: paused the canary and reverted session budget to 1024 at 11:38 PT. observed p95 return to baseline after ~6min warm-up. :thumbsup:
Lena: next steps — I'll open an RFC proposing two changes: 1) make dynamic token budget decision depend on recent kv_hit_rate (so low KV hit => don't shrink budgets), 2) add canary gating that watches kernel-selection drift and auto-rolls-back if p95 delta > 10% relative to baseline.
Taylor: add a perf test to the CI perf-suite that injects low-kv-hit synthetic traffic and asserts no kernel fallback beyond a small threshold.
Ajay: filed INF-4829 with traces, sim configs, and the before/after p95 numbers. linking here for triage.
Maria: thanks all — retagging this thread with #perf #slo #batching and adding the sim configs to the ticket.
